rationale.reason: Hairless sheep/lamb leather is expressly within the linked 4112 branch; uncoated mechanically softened crust remains leather, not a fabricated garment.

reviewed_boundary.scope:
1. Scope and Applicability

This PCR covers a bounded dry mechanical finishing route for hairless sheep or lamb leather: receive already chromium-tanned, retanned, dyed, fat-liquored and dried crust leather at a documented moisture condition suitable for mechanical softening; stake, optionally dry-mill without added chemicals, trim, grade and accept uncoated leather for further garment or glove fabrication. The representative product is dyed sheep nappa without a surface coating. The process sequence and acceptance specification are site and product specific [assomac-finishing; goldpanel-production]. The route begins after upstream wet processing and drying. It excludes raw skins, wet-blue inputs, on-site wet retanning/dyeing/fat-liquoring, deliberate water addition, further thermal drying, coating, buffed suede/nubuck, patent, metallized, composition leather, goats and other species, and manufacture/use of leather articles. Any such operation requires a separately reviewed route expansion with its individual exchanges. CPC 29130 also includes other skins and composition leather; this PCR does not establish coverage of that whole subclass [un-cpc-2025].
reviewed_boundary.covered: Uncoated hairless chrome-tanned dyed sheep/lamb leather from received conditioned crust
reviewed_boundary.excluded: Goat/kid leather; composition leather; wet processing; coatings; synthetic leather; fabricated articles
reviewed_boundary.market_state: Dry saleable leather at declared equilibrium moisture; no fabricated article or lifetime claim

scientific_review.scope: Scope, dry-route representativeness, supplier upstream model, allocation and environmental measurement require independent scientific review.

unresolved_flow_identities.explanation: Public raw sheepskin, wet-blue and mixed finished leather candidates do not establish chromium-tanned dyed fat-liquored dry sheep crust input.

Bounded public search did not establish the exact state, species and composition of Collected chrome-tanned dyed sheep leather fibre dust; retained as an atomic measured exchange, not a claim of database absence.

Public mixed cattle/sheep/pig finished-leather area identity does not establish this uncoated dyed sheep product or a compatible 1 kg reference. Area alone is not a rejection reason: species/state/route and measured conversion remain unestablished.

Bounded public search did not establish the exact state, species and composition of Downgraded uncoated chrome-tanned dyed sheep leather; retained as an atomic measured exchange, not a claim of database absence.

Bounded public search did not establish the exact state, species and composition of Chrome-tanned dyed sheep leather trimmings; retained as an atomic measured exchange, not a claim of database absence.

evidence_limitations: No industry-wide numeric input, energy, yield, moisture or lifetime ranges adopted. All quantities require actual site collection.
Sources establish qualitative route options, not proof that every sheep leather factory uses this route.
Dry mechanical finishing is only a subset of CPC 29130; goat leather, integrated wet processing, coatings and composition leather remain outside coverage.
